ja: 私たちは外で待ってもかまいませんよ。
en: We don't mind waiting outside.
alternatives: We're fine with waiting outside.
Waiting outside is fine with us.
point: mind の後は動名詞。to wait にしない

ja: 田中で予約したテーブルはどこですか？
en: Where's the table reserved under Tanaka?
alternatives: Where is the table booked under Tanaka?
Where's the table we reserved under Tanaka?
point: 「予約した〜」は table のあとに reserved を置く

ja: お水をもう少しいただけますか？
en: Could I have some more water?
alternatives: Can I get some more water?
Could I get a little more water?
point: 丁寧に頼むときは Could I have 〜? で

ja: 予約しておけば、今ごろ並ばずに座れてたのにね。
en: If we'd booked, we'd be seated by now.
alternatives: If we'd reserved, we wouldn't be waiting in line now.
If we'd made a reservation, we'd be sitting down now.
point: 過去の条件は had + 過去分詞、今の結果は would be

ja: ここでいちばん人気の料理は何ですか？
en: What's the most popular dish here?
alternatives: What's your most popular dish?
Which dish is most popular here?
point: 「いちばん人気の」は the most popular で表す

ja: デザートは食後に出していただけますか？
en: Could the dessert be served after the meal?
alternatives: Could you serve dessert after the meal?
Can dessert be brought out after we eat?
point: 出す人を言わない丁寧な頼み方は be served の受動態

ja: 会計が済んだら、外で合流するね。
en: Once I've paid, I'll meet you outside.
alternatives: I'll meet you outside after I pay.
When I'm done paying, I'll join you outside.
point: Once 節は完了を表す現在完了、未来でも will は使わない

ja: すみません、その席はたった今埋まりました。
en: I'm afraid that table was just taken.
alternatives: Sorry, that table has just been taken.
I'm sorry, but that table just got taken.
point: 「席が取られた」は受動態。I'm afraid で柔らかく断る

ja: おすすめは何か教えてもらえますか？
en: Could you tell me what you recommend?
alternatives: Can you tell me what you'd recommend?
Would you mind telling me what you recommend?
point: what 節の中は疑問文の語順にしない（what you recommend）

ja: 店員さんが、9時に閉店だと言ってたよ。
en: The server said they close at nine.
alternatives: The waiter said they close at nine.
The server told us they close at nine.
point: said の後でも今も変わらない事実は現在形でよい

ja: 決められなくて、私は店員さんのおすすめにした。
en: Unable to decide, I went with the server's recommendation.
alternatives: I couldn't decide, so I went with the server's recommendation.
I couldn't decide, so I went with the server's pick.
point: go with で「〜に決める」。分詞構文で理由を前に置く

ja: これ、ニンニク入ってるか分かりますか？
en: Do you know if this has garlic?
alternatives: Can you tell me if this has garlic?
Do you know whether this contains garlic?
point: 知りたい内容は if 節で続け、語順は平叙文

ja: ここが、待つ価値があると友達が言ってた店だよ。
en: This is the place my friend said was worth the wait.
alternatives: This is the restaurant my friend said was worth waiting for.
This is where my friend said the wait was worth it.
point: the place の後ろの関係代名詞は省略。said の後に主語なし

ja: 僕らが着いたときには、もう閉店してた。
en: By the time we arrived, they'd already closed.
alternatives: They had already closed when we got there.
They'd already closed by the time we got there.
point: 着いた時点より前の出来事は過去完了で言う

ja: 席が空いたら、すぐご案内しますね。
en: We'll seat you once a table opens up.
alternatives: We'll seat you when a table frees up.
We'll seat you as soon as one's free.
point: 未来のことでも once / when の節は現在形

ja: 私たち、窓際の席に移らせてもらえないでしょうか？
en: I was wondering if we could move to the window.
alternatives: Would it be possible to move to a window table?
Could we possibly move to a window table?
point: I was wondering if we could で控えめに頼む

ja: クーポンを使っていれば、もっと安かったのにね。
en: If we'd used the coupon, it'd have been cheaper.
alternatives: It would've been cheaper if we'd used the coupon.
We'd have saved money with that coupon.
point: 過去の仮定は if + had 過去分詞、結果は would have

ja: あの店は、料理だけでなく接客も素晴らしかった。
en: Not only was the food great, but the service was excellent.
alternatives: The food was great, and the service was excellent too.
Both the food and the service were excellent.
point: Not only を文頭に出すと was the food と倒置になる

ja: お腹すいた。ランチにしよう。
en: I'm hungry. Let's have lunch.
alternatives: I'm starving. Let's get lunch.
I'm starving. Let's eat lunch.
point: lunch には a を付けない

ja: 私たち、遅れたら席を取っておいてもらえますか？
en: If we're late, could you hold our table?
alternatives: Could you hold our table if we run late?
If we run late, would you keep our table?
point: If 節は未来のことでも現在形。hold は「取り置く」

ja: あの店のカレー、辛すぎて涙が出たよ。
en: That curry was so hot it made my eyes water.
alternatives: That curry was so spicy it made me cry.
That curry was so spicy I teared up.
point: 「涙が出る」は make my eyes water。使役の make を使う

ja: 一度食べてから、この料理がずっと食べたかったんだ。
en: I've wanted this dish ever since I tried it.
alternatives: I've been craving this dish since I first tried it.
I haven't stopped wanting this dish since I tried it.
point: since の主節は現在完了、since 節は過去形

ja: 新しくできたラーメン屋、もう行った？
en: Have you tried that new ramen place yet?
alternatives: Have you checked out that new ramen place?
Have you been to the new ramen shop?
point: 「もう〜した？」は現在完了の疑問文＋ yet

ja: ワインはソムリエに選ばせれば、まず外れないよ。
en: Have the sommelier pick the wine and you can't go wrong.
alternatives: Let the sommelier choose the wine and you can't go wrong.
Leave the wine to the sommelier and you can't go wrong.
point: 「選ばせる」は have / let＋人＋動詞の原形。can't go wrong は失敗しない

ja: 窓際の席に座ってもいいですか？
en: May I sit by the window?
alternatives: Could I sit by the window?
Can I sit by the window?
point: 「〜してもいいですか」は May I 〜? で丁寧に許可を求める

ja: お皿を下げるよう店員さんに頼んで。
en: Ask the waiter to clear these.
alternatives: Ask the server to clear these.
Ask the waiter to take these away.
point: ask + 人 + to do の形。that 節にしない

ja: 私たち、もう30分も待ってるんですけど。
en: We've been waiting half an hour already.
alternatives: We've been waiting for thirty minutes now.
We've already waited half an hour.
point: 待ち続けている今の状態は have been -ing

ja: 彼があの店に行かなくなったのは、接客のせいだよ。
en: It was the service that drove him away.
alternatives: What drove him away was the service.
It was the service that made him stop going.
The service is what made him stop going.
point: 理由を It was と that で挟んで強調。drive away で「足が遠のく」

ja: あそこは先に予約しないとだめだよ。
en: You have to book ahead there.
alternatives: You need to book ahead there.
You need a reservation there.
point: 「〜しないといけない」は have to＋動詞の原形

ja: 私たちは、ここのケーキを食べに来た。
en: We came here to eat the cake.
alternatives: We came to try the cake here.
We came here for the cake.
point: 「食べるために」は to 不定詞で目的を表す

ja: 姉は寿司が大好きだが、私は生魚が苦手なんだ。
en: My sister loves sushi, but raw fish isn't my thing.
alternatives: My sister loves sushi, but I can't handle raw fish.
My sister adores sushi, but I'm not into raw fish.
point: 「苦手」は isn't my thing や not into。対比は but でよい

ja: このお店、カードで払えますか？
en: Can I pay by card here?
alternatives: Do you take cards here?
Can I pay with a card?
point: 「カードで」は by card。by の後は冠詞なし

ja: このパスタ、前回よりずっとおいしい。
en: This is much better than last time.
alternatives: This is way better than last time.
This tastes much better than last time.
point: 「ずっと」は比較級の前に much や way を置く

ja: 私、すごく辛い料理は食べられません。
en: I can't eat very spicy food.
alternatives: I can't handle very spicy food.
I can't eat anything very spicy.
point: 「食べられない」は can't eat。handle も自然

ja: 現金のみだって、先に知っていればよかった。
en: I wish I'd known it was cash only.
alternatives: I wish I'd known earlier it was cash only.
If only I'd known they only take cash.
point: 過去への後悔は wish の後を had + 過去分詞にする

ja: 店員さんが押さえると言った席、どれか分かる？
en: Do you know which table the server said they'd hold?
alternatives: Do you know which table the server said they'd keep?
Do you know which table the waiter said they'd save?
point: 間接疑問は which table のあとも肯定文の語順

ja: お金を気にしなくていいなら、私ならコースを頼むな。
en: If money were no object, I'd order the full course.
alternatives: If cost weren't an issue, I'd get the full course.
If price didn't matter, I'd get the full course.
point: 現実と違う仮定は if + were、主節は would

ja: 私たち二人で分けられる料理はありますか？
en: Is there a dish we can share?
alternatives: Do you have a dish we can share?
Is there something we can split?
point: a dish の後ろに we can share をそのままつなぐ

ja: 着いたら、日替わりはもう売り切れてた。
en: The daily special had sold out when we arrived.
alternatives: When we got there, the special had sold out.
The special was already gone when we got there.
point: 着く前に売り切れ済み。先に起きたことは had + 過去分詞

ja: あの店員さん、注文を聞き間違えたに違いないよ。
en: That server must have misheard our order.
alternatives: That server must have gotten our order wrong.
The server must have gotten our order mixed up.
point: 過去の確信ある推量は must have + 過去分詞

ja: この店、閉店したと聞いたけど、まだやってるじゃん。
en: I heard this place had closed, but it's still open.
alternatives: They said this place had closed, yet it's still open.
I heard it had shut down, but it's still open.
point: 聞いた時点より前の閉店は過去完了、今の状態は現在形
